n10.vanliga-missforstand.2: Eight statements that sound reasonable. Think about what is wrong before you open them.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.3: “A question only activates part of the weights.”
n10.vanliga-missforstand.4: In a dense model every weight is used for every token. What varies are the activations. Only in MoE are parts of the weights selected, and then per token and layer, not per question.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.6: Chatting never changes the weights. The whole conversation is sent in again every time. The KV cache and prefix caching only mean it does not have to be recomputed.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.7: “The KV cache is an approximation that trades quality for speed.”
n10.vanliga-missforstand.8: An unquantized cache reuses mathematically identical K and V: the causal mask prevents new tokens from affecting earlier positions. Floating-point rounding can still cause small logit differences. A quantized cache is an approximation.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.10: Greedy removes the randomness in sampling, but floating-point ordering can differ between batches and flip a close argmax.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.11: “The experts in an MoE model are subject-matter experts.”
n10.vanliga-missforstand.12: The split is learned and varies across models and layers. Mixtral often showed syntactic patterns, but this does not rule out topic-related patterns in other models. An expert number is not a guaranteed topic label.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.13: “A reasoning model has a different architecture.”
n10.vanliga-missforstand.14: The same transformer. It is trained to write out a reasoning chain first, which costs more decode steps.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.15: “A larger batch makes every step proportionally slower.”
n10.vanliga-missforstand.16: Decode is memory-bound. The weights are read once per step regardless of batch, so throughput grows almost linearly for a good while.
n10.vanliga-missforstand.17: “nvidia-smi shows 90% memory, the server is nearly full.”
n10.vanliga-missforstand.18: vLLM allocates the whole KV pool at startup. Look at vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc to see how much is actually in use.
n10.fusklapp.1: Cheat sheet: formulas, shapes and numbers
n10.fusklapp.60: Prefill often becomes compute-bound once T is large enough; short prefill can be memory-bound. Small-batch decode is usually memory-bound.
n10.fusklapp.61: The weights decide whether the model fits. The KV cache decides how many users fit.
n10.fusklapp.62: Anything shared by many (weights, prefixes) should be read or computed once. That is what an inference engine does.
n10.slutprov.2: Twelve questions from the whole course. The explanation appears right after each answer.
